newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes tick higher, cash grades remain steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes tick higher, cash grades remain steady.

text.p: U.S. crudes talked late Tuesday at slightly firmer levels for outright barrels, while domestic grade differentials remained steady.

Traders said continued problems in returning Canada's Interprovincial Pipe Line to full throughput capacity aided the complex, but domestic grades were burdened with competition from foreign offerings.

May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 10 cents higher at $19.35-45 a barrel, trading in the U.S. aftermarket window for outright deals at $19.40. The May/June WTI roll stayed put at a 10 cts advantage for the second month.
